This Finger Lake is the longest, some 40 miles long, though it has only the second-largest surface area.
This lake, namesake of a utopian commune founded by John Noyes, is not a Finger Lake but is referred to as "the thumb."

bonuses.leadin: Members of this group include Lakes Skaneateles, Owasco, Keuka, and Canandaigua. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this rival of future pope Julius II, who divided the New World between Spain and Portugal after his election in 1492.
Alexander VI was part of this infamous Spanish-Italian family. Other members of this family included the rumoured poisoner Lucrezia.
A French king of this name, nicknamed "the Affable," invaded Italy during Alexander VI's papacy. Another king of this name won the Hundred Years' War against Britain.

bonuses.leadin: [NOTE TO MODERATOR: Do NOT reveal alternate answer lines to the first bonus part unless given by the team.] This Pope made his son Cesare a cardinal, but his son later resigned that office. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this democratically elected left wing leader of Chile who was overthrown in a 1973 US backed coup by Augusto Pinochet.
After overthrowing Allende, Pinochet helped establish this project which involved the CIA helping support right wing South American governments. Argentina's Dirty War was part of this project.

This country's former president Joao Goulart was assassinated as part of Operation Condor. Goulart was the last left wing president of this country before Lula da Silva, who defeated Jair Bolsonaro in a 2022 election.

bonuses.leadin: The Caravan of Death was a death squad that carried out executions after the overthrow of this leader. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This King of Wessex ruled from 871 to 900. He patronized the scholars Asser and Erigena and translated several Latin texts himself.
The bad advice he received and constant Viking invasions helped give this king, who reigned from 978 to 1016, the nickname "the Unready."
This founder of Westminster Abbey died in 1066, and controversy erupted as to whether he intended to honor a deal with William of Normandy.

bonuses.leadin: Name these Anglo-Saxon kings of England for 10 points each.

parts.text: This organization funded by the Nixon administration laundered money and utilized illegal slush funds to fund the Watergate burglars, among other shady activities.
This false name was given to the secret informant of Washington Post reporter Bob Woodward, later revealed to be senior FBI agent W. Mark Felt Sr.
This man was the chief operative for the White House Plumbers and took control of planning the Watergate break-in along with E. Howard Hunt.

parts.text: Name these devices. ES&S, Dominion, and Hart InterCivic are three companies that have a virtual monopoly on selling these devices in the United States.
In this year, Ohio's secretary-of-state controversially offered a $100 million contract to Diebold Election Systems, whose president also voted Republican. George W. Bush was re-elected in this year.
The push for voting machines came after 2000, during which some of these objects were left partially attached to ballot cards in Florida, so votes were not properly tabulated.

bonuses.leadin: In 2005, Harri Hursti demonstrated a flaw in these devices using his namesake "hack". For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this devastating fire in eastern Wisconsin that was overshadowed by the Great Chicago Fire that took place on the same day. It currently remains the deadliest firestorm in American history by number of lives lost.

This congressman and notable pseudoscientist claimed that both the Great Chicago Fire and the Peshtigo fire were caused by Biela's comet. He theorized civilizations were descended from the title society in his book Atlantis: The Antediluvian World. More seriously, he wrote the preamble for the Omaha platform.
The Omaha platform was the program of this party in 1892, which nominated James Weaver for the presidency. It shifted to a more single-issue, pro-free silver platform four years later.

He ended his career as missionary to the Indians at Stockbridge, where he completed The Great Christian Doctrine of Original Sin Defended.

Both Whitefield and Edwards were attacked by this Boston divine, whose 1742 sermon Enthusiasm Described and Cautioned Against saw in the Awakening the legacy of the Munster Anabaptists and Antinomians.

The Spartacist League was put down by the right-wing Freikorps on the orders of Friedrich Ebert, who led this government. This government led post-WWI Germany through a period of hyperinflation.

This American general commanded an outnumbered forward guard at Monmouth and later took Stony Point. After the Revolution, he defeated Little Turtle and Blue Jacket at the Battle of Fallen Timbers.

Artisans of the Ming Dynasty made blue-and-white ceramics using this material, which they made in a kiln.

The Chicago Police Department falsely claimed to the media that Hampton had been killed during a chaotic gunfight with members of this civil rights activist organization named for a type of wild cat. No such gunfight occurred.

This FCC rule required stations to present multiple viewpoints when discussing controversial issues. Unlike the equal-time rule, this doctrine was abolished in 1987.

One of the inaugural FCC commissioners, Norman Case, also served as governor of this state. Longtime senators from this state include Theodore F. Green and Claiborne Pell, the namesake of the Pell Grant.

France reconquered Normandy from England at this war's Battle of Formigny (FOR-meen-yee). Henry V (the fifth) was victorious in this war's Battle of Agincourt (AH-jin-kor).
This Viking, who was baptized as Robert I (the first), was the first Duke of Normandy. He often clashed with Charles the Simple.
